name: Student Management System
tagline: Keep student records, courses, enrollments and attendance in a SQLite database, with a Flask web interface.
description: A Python web application built with Flask and SQLite. It manages students, courses, enrollments and daily attendance, with search, filters, sorting, pages and statistics. Every query uses SQL parameters, every form is protected against cross-site request forgery, and the database enforces its relationships with foreign keys and cascading deletes. The pages need no JavaScript, and the database is one file on your own computer.
features: Add, view, edit and delete students, with validation of every field and a confirmation page before anything is deleted.
Search students by name, roll number or email; filter by class and status; sort by name, roll number, class or admission date; move through pages.
Add, edit and delete courses, and see the students and attendance in each one.
Enroll students in courses and remove them; a student's attendance in a course goes with the enrollment.
Mark each student present, late or absent for a course on any day up to today, and change the marks later.
Statistics calculated from the data: students by status and class, and attendance per course.
CSRF protection on every form, SQL parameters for every query, escaped output and security headers.
Database commands to back up, reset and refill the database, and a fictional sample class for the first run.
limitations: There is no login: anyone who can open the app can change the records.
Designed for one person on one computer, with Flask's development server and SQLite.
Attendance has one mark per course per day, not per lecture.
Times such as “Last updated” are shown in UTC.
There is no import or export; back up by copying the database file.
learningObjectives: Design a relational database with primary keys, foreign keys, a many-to-many relationship and constraints.
Write SQL for CRUD operations, joins, aggregates and upserts, safely with parameters.
Build a server-rendered web app with Flask routes, blueprints, templates and forms.
Validate input and protect forms against cross-site request forgery.
Test a web app and its database with pytest and Flask's test client.
ideasForExtension: Add a login with hashed passwords, so only staff can change records.
Import students from a CSV file, with validation of every row.
Export the attendance of a course as a CSV file.
Add a timetable with lectures, and mark attendance per lecture.

prerequisites.name: Python
prerequisites.note: On Windows, tick “Add python.exe to PATH” during installation.

prerequisites.name: A modern web browser
prerequisites.note: The app runs at http://127.0.0.1:5000/ on your own computer.

steps.title: Create and activate a virtual environment
steps.note: If PowerShell blocks the activation script, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned once and try again.

steps.title: Install the dependencies
steps.note: Needs an internet connection the first time. Flask and its dependencies are a few megabytes.

steps.title: Start the app
steps.note: Open http://127.0.0.1:5000/ in your browser. The first start creates instance/students.db with the sample data. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop.

notes: The database is the file instance/students.db. Back it up with flask --app studentms backup-db, and start again with flask --app studentms reset-db --yes.
Change the app name, institution, page size and sample data in app_config.json, and the port or database location in a .env file (see .env.example).
If port 5000 is busy (on macOS, AirPlay Receiver uses it), set PORT to another number before python run.py.
Activate the virtual environment again each time you open a new terminal.

covers: Every validation rule for students, courses and attendance dates.
Configuration, .env loading and the secret key.
Queries: search, filters, sorting, pages, enrollments, attendance upserts and statistics.
Database constraints, unique values and cascading deletes.
Every page through Flask's test client: adding, editing and deleting students and courses, enrolling and marking attendance.
The backup, reset and seed commands, and security: CSRF tokens, escaping, SQL injection attempts and headers.

variables.name: SECRET_KEY
variables.description: Signs the session cookie. Leave it unset and the app creates a random key in instance/secret_key.

variables.name: PORT
variables.description: The port the app listens on (default 5000).

variables.name: DATABASE_PATH
variables.description: Where the database file is (default instance/students.db).

stack.summary: python run.py starts Flask's development server on your own computer. Each page is made on the server from the SQLite database file instance/students.db and sent to your browser as HTML; nothing leaves your computer.

network.notes: pip install downloads Flask once. The app then runs locally and makes no network requests.
